description: Standard response envelope for all bridge-dispatched probes. Every bridge response should end with a structured summary block that enables instant context recovery on resume.
purpose: When the dispatch loop resumes the agent, the agent needs to instantly know what each response WAS and what it MEANS without reading the full response. This schema defines the summary block that every bridge prompt should request.

response_summary_block.description: Appended to the end of every bridge response. The observe plan runner extracts this and injects it into the resume continue instruction.

teleology.constraint: One sentence. What this response IS — its purpose and what it contains.
examples: Structured review of 7 Lab P1 miner prompts with per-miner improvement suggestions.
Cross-target correlation matrix for the measurements dossier with 6 stable and 4 regime-dependent pairs.
Delta analysis of Oracle run RUN_2026-03-06 identifying 3 OBSERVATION_MISS patterns in measurements lane.

outcome.constraint: One sentence. What the agent should DO with this response.
examples: Merge the correlation data into codex/substrate/dossiers/measurements.json under CROSS_ASSET_CORRELATIONS.
Generate dossier patches for measurements.json targeting INSTITUTIONAL_FLOW section.

confidence.constraint: How confident the response is in its analysis. HIGH = well-grounded in provided context. MEDIUM = some inference required. LOW = speculative or context was thin.

prompt_suffix.description: Add this to the end of every bridge prompt to request the summary block.
prompt_suffix.template:
[RESPONSE SUMMARY — REQUIRED]
End your response with this exact JSON block:
```json
{"_summary": {"teleology": "one sentence: what this response IS", "outcome": "one sentence: what to DO with it", "confidence": "HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW"}}
```
This block is extracted by the dispatch system for resume context. Keep each field to one sentence.

extraction_rules.description: How the observe plan runner extracts the summary from the response.
rules: Search for {"_summary": ...} JSON block in the response text (last occurrence wins).
If no _summary block found, fall back to the first 100 chars of the response.
